why: The conclusions agree: A's 'sc-Banach Q with a level-wise surjective sc-operator q : E → Q, ker q_m = A_m' gives B's level-wise isomorphisms Q_m ≃L E_m/A_m intertwining the inclusions (the induced maps E_m/A_m → Q_m are continuous bijections of Banach spaces, inverted by the open mapping theorem), and conversely q_m := φ_m⁻¹ ∘ mk (B_to_A_scSubspace, proved with B). The genuine difference is the hypothesis: A (proposition_1_1_8) assumes only that A is closed, B (the text) that A is an sc-subspace; B says nothing about closed subspaces that are not sc-subspaces (e.g. the span of a non-smooth vector), so B ⇒ A is not derivable from B, only by re-proving A outright. No universe parameters.
B_issue: None of substance. The blind author reads the text's E_m/A_m = {(x+A) ∩ E_m : x ∈ E} with x ∈ E_m (the literal x ∈ E₀ would add ∅) and uses the abstract quotient E_m ⧸ A_m with level-wise isomorphisms, which is the intended notion.
